doc.title: Donn Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 6, 2009

title: Playing Carnegie Hall
summary: The Carnegie Hall concert came through Dave Cook and Jim Carpenter; the turnout from Hamilton was modest.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Yeah, we got that job through the auspices of a fellow named Dave Cook, a clarinet player with the Dartmouth Indian Chiefs, which was a band that was one of our — I wouldn’t say rivals because we operated in a different market. But he had suggested to Jim Carpenter, who was running these college jazz bands that go to Carnegie Hall that we were a pretty good band and give us a try. So we did and they did, and we ended up playing opposite an all-star band from the Central Plaza in New York. We played two sets each and then had one set together. And that was quite an experience.
Standing on the stage at Carnegie Hall. Great things have happened here, people who have stood on the stage.
Did the college take note of that?

Yes, they did, but not really as much as I would have liked. It was over Thanksgiving holiday and people could have gone but we didn’t have a good showing from Hamilton people, and from my high school I would say that Carnegie Hall was not full by any means.
